note: Rotation library for the Strumica valley. A rotation is a list of seasons (October to September). Each season lists the crops sown in it, in order: a winter cover crop sown in October comes before the summer crop it protects. The rotation repeats. 'common' = what many farms in the valley grow today.

rotations.name: Pepper → pepper → tomato
rotations.idea: The usual vegetable sequence in the valley: high income, but three nightshades in a row and bare winters.

rotations.name: Pepper → pepper → tomato, with winter vetch
rotations.idea: Keeps the same cash crops but covers the soil every winter with vetch and oats.

rotations.name: Pepper → wheat → bean, vetch before pepper
rotations.idea: Breaks the nightshade cycle with a cereal and a legume; the vetch adds nitrogen before the pepper.

rotations.name: Pepper → wheat → chickpea → tomato
rotations.idea: Two vegetable years out of four; chickpea needs little water and fixes nitrogen.

rotations.name: Alfalfa (2 years) → maize → pepper
rotations.idea: Deep alfalfa roots rebuild soil structure and nitrogen; the field is covered almost all year.

rotations.name: Tomato → wheat → sunflower
rotations.idea: A lower-water rotation: sunflower and wheat are grown without irrigation.

rotations.name: Tobacco → wheat → bean
rotations.idea: Common on the drier fields at the valley edge.

rotations.name: Maize → wheat → bean
rotations.idea: A field-crop rotation without vegetables: less labour, lower income.

rotations.name: Wheat → chickpea
rotations.idea: Wheat with a chickpea break: a rain-fed legume that adds nitrogen and stops cereal diseases carrying over.

rotations.name: Wheat → sunflower → chickpea, vetch before sunflower
rotations.idea: Three field crops from three plant families, all workable without irrigation, with the soil covered over winter.

rotations.name: Wheat → maize → bean, vetch before maize
rotations.idea: Keeps wheat and maize, adds a bean year and a winter cover so the soil is not bare before maize.

rotations.name: Alfalfa (2 years) → wheat → sunflower
rotations.idea: A two-year alfalfa ley rebuilds soil structure and nitrogen, then feeds the cereals that follow.
